'''Vittorio Prodi''' (19 May 1937 – 29 July 2023) was an Italian politician who served as a [[member of the European Parliament]] from 2004 until 2014. He was a member of the [[Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats]].

== Biography ==
Prodi was born in [[Reggio Emilia]] in 1937, and was one of the former prime minister [[Romano Prodi]]'s eight siblings. In the [[European Parliament]], Prodi served on the [[Committee on Industry, Research and Energy]]. He was also a substitute for the [[European Parliament Committee on the Environment, Public Health and Food Safety]], a member of the Delegation for relations with the United States, and a substitute for the Delegation for relations with the People's Republic of China. He represented the European Parliament at the [[2008 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] in [[Poznań]], Poland.<ref>Jennifer Rankin (November 26, 2008), [http://www.politico.eu/article/meps-flock-to-poznan-meeting/ MEPs flock to Poznań meeting] ''[[European Voice]]''.</ref> He died on 29 July 2023, at the age of 86.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://bologna.repubblica.it/cronaca/2023/07/30/news/e_morto_vittorio_prodi_fratello_di_romano_ed_ex_parlamentare_europeo-409452738/?ref=RHUO-UO|title=È morto Vittorio Prodi, fratello di Romano ed ex parlamentare europeo|work=La Repubblica|language=it|date=30 July 2023|access-date=30 July 2023}}</ref>

=== Career ===
* 1959: [[Graduate school|Graduated]] in [[physics]] at the [[University of Bologna]]
* 1970: [[lecturer]] in nuclear measurements
* since 1983: associate [[professor]] in the Physics Department of the [[University of Bologna]]
* 1995–2004: [[President of the Province of Bologna]]
* 2001–2004: Member of the provincial representation of the conference State – Cities – Local Governments and of the Unified Conference (State, Cities, Local Governments, and Regions)
* Author of numerous publications and of five international patents
